info.title: AgentAPI Proxy
info.description: API for managing agent sessions, schedules, and settings. AgentAPI Proxy provides a unified interface for running AI agents with Kubernetes-based session management.

get.description: Returns token usage totals for the authenticated user, or for an accessible team when team_id is supplied.

403.description: Not authorized for the requested team

get.summary: Export filtered usage events as Parquet
get.description: Returns authorized raw usage events for local analytics with DuckDB-Wasm. Defaults to 30 days; the maximum range is 90 days and the maximum result is 100000 events.

403.description: Not authorized for the requested scope

post.description: Stores idempotent response-level token usage events reported by a session Stop hook. Session ownership is resolved by the server.

200.description: Events stored or identified as duplicates

get.description: Returns the health status of the proxy server.

post.description: Creates a new session and starts an agentapi server instance. Returns a stable public session ID for subsequent requests. When allocation selects a different concrete session ID, the returned ID remains a routable alias for the lifetime of the session.

session_id.description: Stable public session identifier (UUID). This ID remains valid even when the concrete allocated session has a different ID.

get.description: Returns a list of sessions. Non-admin users can see their own sessions and team-scoped sessions they have access to. Supports filtering by status, scope, team, and tags.

delete.summary: Delete a session or pending session allocation
delete.description: Terminates and deletes a session, or cancels a pending session allocation. Users can only delete their own sessions and allocations.

200.description: Session or pending session allocation deleted successfully

403.description: Forbidden - can only delete own sessions

409.description: Session allocation is no longer pending

post.description: Explicitly recreates the runtime workload for a suspended session. Read-only status, message, and SSE requests do not resume sessions.

501.description: Resume is not supported by the configured session manager

get.description: Opens a Server-Sent Events stream that pushes a `SessionStatusEvent` whenever any session accessible to the authenticated user changes status. A heartbeat comment (`: heartbeat`) is sent every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive. The stream stays open until the client disconnects.

200.description: SSE stream of SessionStatusEvent objects. Each event line: `data: {"session_id":"...","status":"...","timestamp":"..."}`

501.description: Not implemented for this session manager type

get.description: Blocks until any session accessible to the authenticated user changes status, or until the timeout expires. Returns a `SessionStatusEvent` on change, or `{"events": []}` on timeout.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum wait time in seconds (default: 30, max: 60).

200.description: A `SessionStatusEvent` if a status change occurred before the timeout, or `{"events": []}` if the timeout elapsed with no change.

501.description: Not implemented for this session manager type

get.summary: Long-poll for message updates in a session
get.description: Blocks until a `message_update` event is received from the agentapi backend for the specified session, or until the timeout expires. Returns `{"updated": true, "session_id": "...", "timestamp": "..."}` on update, or `{"updated": false}` on timeout. Clients should immediately re-issue the request after each response to maintain continuous notification.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Maximum wait time in seconds (default: 30, max: 60).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Timestamp of the last known message update. If the session has received a message_update after this time, the response is returned immediately without waiting. Accepts Unix timestamp in milliseconds (integer) or RFC3339 string. Use the `timestamp` value from the previous response.

200.description: A message update occurred, a catch-up update was detected via `since`, or the timeout elapsed.

501.description: Not implemented for this session manager type

get.summary: Get aggregated domains for a sandbox policy
get.description: Returns the allowed/denied/ignored domain lists collected by the background domain collector from all sessions using this policy. Data is refreshed every 60 seconds. Returns empty lists when no data has been collected yet.

ignored.description: Domains the user has chosen to ignore (not shown as suggestions)

updated_at.description: When the data was last collected

put.summary: Update the ignored domain list for a sandbox policy
put.description: Replaces the ignored domain list stored in the collected domain data for the given policy. Ignored domains are suppressed from the import suggestion UI so users are not repeatedly prompted to act on them.

ignored.description: Full list of domains to ignore

get.summary: Get domains accessed by a sandboxed session
get.description: Returns the list of domains that the session's network filter proxy has seen, split into allowed (accessed) and denied (blocked) sets. Only available for Kubernetes sessions with a sandbox sidecar. Returns 503 when the network filter is not running.

200.description: Domain lists from the network filter

allowed.description: Domains that were allowed through the filter

denied.description: Domains that were blocked by the filter

501.description: Not implemented for this session type

503.description: Network filter not available for this session

Creates a new memory entry for a user or team. User-scoped memories are private to the owner. Team-scoped memories are accessible to all team members.

get.description: Lists memory entries accessible to the authenticated user. User-scoped queries return only the user's own entries. Team-scoped queries return entries for teams the user belongs to.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by scope: 'user' or 'team'. Omit to return both.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Filter by team ID (required when scope=team)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search query applied to title and content (case-insensitive)

parameters.name: include_tag.{key}
parameters.description: Include only memories whose tags contain ALL of the specified key=value pairs. For example, `include_tag.category=news` returns only memories tagged with `category=news`. Multiple include_tag parameters are AND-combined.

parameters.name: exclude_tag.{key}
parameters.description: Exclude memories whose tags contain ALL of the specified key=value pairs. For example, `exclude_tag.category=news` excludes memories tagged with `category=news`. Multiple exclude_tag parameters are AND-combined.

get.description: Retrieves a specific memory entry by ID. Access is restricted to the owner (user-scoped) or team members (team-scoped). Admin privilege does NOT bypass these restrictions.

put.description: Updates a memory entry. Only the owner (user-scoped) or team members (team-scoped) can update. Omitted fields are not changed.

delete.description: Deletes a memory entry. Only the owner (user-scoped) or team members (team-scoped) can delete.

post.description: Transfers ownership of a user- or team-scoped resource. Supports dry-run validation.

get.summary: Get Codex device auth configuration status
get.description: Returns whether Codex device authentication is configured on this proxy instance.

post.description: Runs `codex login --device-auth` and returns the user code and verification URI for the user to complete authentication in their browser.

post.description: Returns the current status of the caller's in-progress device auth session. The session is identified by the caller's authentication token.

get.description: Lists named API tokens accessible to the authenticated user. Personal (user-scoped) tokens are strictly owner-only. Team-scoped tokens are visible to team members. The plaintext secret is never returned; each item only exposes a short token_prefix.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by scope: 'personal' or 'team'. Omit to return both the caller's personal tokens and tokens for teams the caller belongs to.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Filter by team ID (required when scope=team)

post.description: Creates a new named, revocable API token. Personal tokens authenticate as the owner; team tokens authenticate as a team-scoped service account. The plaintext secret is returned exactly once in the response. The response carries Cache-Control: no-store. Requested permissions cannot be broader than the caller's permissions; when omitted they default to the caller's own session permissions (never granting a permission the caller lacks). Team tokens require team membership (admins qualify). Name is required (1..64 characters after trimming). Scope uses the public vocabulary 'personal' (default) or 'team'.

201.description: API token created. The plaintext token is included exactly once in the `plaintext_token` field; metadata is nested under `token`.

Cache-Control.description: Always 'no-store' to prevent caching the secret.

get.description: Returns metadata for a single API token. The plaintext secret is never returned. A 404 is returned both when the token does not exist and when the caller is not authorized to view it, so existence across scopes is not leaked.

delete.description: Deletes (revokes) an API token. Personal tokens can only be deleted by the owner. Team tokens can be deleted by the creator or an admin. The operation is idempotent: a 204 is returned for nonexistent or not-authorized token IDs without leaking whether the token exists in another scope. Revocation takes effect immediately on the replica handling the delete (in-memory auth map); across other replicas it is eventually consistent via periodic reconciliation with the token store. Global immediate cross-replica revocation is not guaranteed.

204.description: Token deleted (or did not exist / not authorized; idempotent, no content)

get.summary: Long-poll the next External Session Manager allocation
get.description: Internal manager-token-authenticated allocation endpoint. Kubernetes allocations include the parent-owned runtime_profile that the ESM must apply before creating the session.

parameters.name: profile_revision
parameters.description: Last runtime profile revision applied by the ESM. A mismatch ends the long-poll immediately and returns the current revision header.

200.description: Allocation claimed for the authenticated manager

runtime_profile.description: Versioned NFA, SCIA, and session identity configuration inherited from the parent proxy. ESM-local overrides are not supported.

204.description: Long-poll timeout or runtime profile revision mismatch

get.summary: Get the parent runtime profile snapshot
get.description: Returns the current content-addressed runtime profile after the allocation long-poll reports a new revision.

tags.description: Tags for the session (e.g., repository, branch). Keys prefixed with allocator. select an External Session Manager by exact label match; multiple allocator.* tags use AND semantics. allocator.id matches the manager ID.

scope.description: Ownership scope of the session (default: user)

memory_key.description: Custom tag map to identify memories for this session. If not specified or empty, the session tags are used as the memory key. If both are empty, memory integration is disabled.

resume_from.description: Previous proxy session ID whose persisted ACP conversation state should be restored before starting the agent

message.description: Initial message to send to the agent after session starts

github_token.description: GitHub token to use for authentication instead of GitHub App

agent_type.description: Agent type for the session. Supported values include 'auto', 'claude-acp', 'codex-acp', and 'cursor'. 'auto' selects codex-acp when Codex auth.json is available, otherwise claude-acp. If not specified, uses default agentapi.

oneshot.description: When true, the session will automatically delete itself after Claude stops responding. Uses Claude Code Stop hook to execute session deletion.

initial_message_wait_second.description: Number of seconds to wait after the agent becomes stable before sending the initial message. Defaults to 2 seconds if not specified.

cycle_message.description: Message to send to the session after each Claude stop event. When set, a Stop hook is injected into the session's Claude settings that runs `agentapi-proxy client cycle <message>`. The cycle continues until /tmp/check/CYCLE_OK exists or cycle_max_count is reached.

cycle_max_count.description: Maximum number of cycles to run. 0 means unlimited. Requires cycle_message to be set. The current count is tracked in /tmp/check/CYCLE_COUNT inside the session.

session_ttl.description: Duration after the last message before this session is automatically deleted. Accepted format: Go duration string (e.g. '48h', '168h', '7d' is not valid — use hours). Empty string means the global cleanup worker TTL is used for Slackbot sessions; non-Slackbot sessions without this field are not auto-deleted.

unsynced_file_paths.description: Managed file paths that should not be synced back to storage from this session.

credential_source.description: Managed credential files to inject. session_user uses the trigger configuration owner, triggered_user uses the rendered username tag and falls back to team credentials, team uses the session team, and none disables credential injection. When omitted, user-scoped sessions use session_user and team-scoped sessions use none.

DockerParams.description: Docker-in-Docker (DinD) configuration for the session. When enabled, a privileged DinD sidecar is injected into the session Pod and DOCKER_HOST is set so the main container can run docker commands.

enabled.description: When true, a DinD sidecar (docker:dind) is added to the session Pod and DOCKER_HOST=tcp://127.0.0.1:2375 is set in the main container.

registries.description: Authenticated container registries. Supports inline credentials (username/password) or a reference to a Kubernetes Secret containing docker config JSON.

DockerRegistry.description: Authentication configuration for a container registry.

server.description: Registry server address (e.g. 'ghcr.io', 'registry.example.com'). Leave empty for Docker Hub.

username.description: Registry username for inline credentials. Used together with password.

password.description: Registry password or access token for inline credentials.

secret_name.description: Name of a Kubernetes Secret containing a 'config.json' key with docker config JSON. When set, this secret is mounted into the DinD container for daemon-level auth. Takes priority over cluster-wide dind_registry_secret_name.

insecure.description: When true, adds --insecure-registry=<server> to the DinD daemon args, allowing plain HTTP communication with this registry.

SandboxParams.description: Network sandbox configuration for the session. When enabled, outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic is routed through a transparent proxy sidecar. allowed_domains (allowlist) takes precedence over denied_domains (denylist). A policy_id may reference a SandboxPolicy resource whose domain lists are merged before session-level overrides.

enabled.description: When true, the network-filter init container and sidecar are injected into the session Pod. The init container configures iptables to redirect HTTP/HTTPS traffic through the sidecar.

policy_id.description: ID of a SandboxPolicy resource to use as the base rule set. The policy's allowed_domains and denied_domains are merged with session-level overrides. Session-level domains take precedence.

allowed_domains.description: Allowlist mode: only listed destinations are permitted; all others are blocked. Supports hostname wildcard prefixes (e.g. '*.example.com'), exact IPv4 addresses, and IPv4 CIDR ranges. IP addresses and CIDR ranges are installed as direct iptables allow rules by the init container. Takes precedence over denied_domains when set.

denied_domains.description: Denylist mode: listed domains are blocked, all others are allowed. Used only when allowed_domains is empty. Supports wildcard prefixes (e.g. '*.example.com').

count_mode.description: When true, enables count mode: policy rules are evaluated and blocked domains are recorded, but traffic is not actually blocked. Useful for auditing policies before enforcing them in production. Requires nfa v0.6.0+.

SandboxPolicy.description: A named, reusable set of network filter rules. Sessions reference a policy by ID; the policy's domain lists are merged with session-level overrides at creation time.

description.example: Allows access to GitHub and npm registry

allowed_domains.description: Allowlist: only these domains are permitted. Supports wildcard prefixes.

denied_domains.description: Denylist: these domains are blocked. Used only when allowed_domains is empty.

count_mode.description: When true, policy rules are evaluated and blocked domains are recorded, but traffic is not actually blocked. Useful for auditing policies before enforcing them in production. Requires nfa v0.6.0+.
When true, enables count mode: policy rules are evaluated and blocked domains are recorded, but traffic is not actually blocked.

pool.description: Automatically managed logical pool for this manager

count_mode.description: When true, enables count mode: policy rules are evaluated and blocked domains are recorded, but traffic is not actually blocked.

WebhookSignatureType.description: Signature verification type: hmac (HMAC-based signature verification, default), static (simple token comparison)

scope.description: Ownership scope of the webhook (default: user)

status.description: Initial status of the webhook (default: active)

secret.description: Custom secret for HMAC signature verification. If not provided, a random secret is auto-generated. Use this to set a pre-shared secret from external services (e.g., Sentry Client Secret).

signature_header.description: Name of the HTTP header containing the signature (default: X-Signature). Useful for services that use different header names like X-Slack-Signature or X-Hub-Signature-256

signature_prefix.description: Prefix to strip from the signature header value before HMAC comparison. When empty, auto-detection is used (strips 'algorithm=' prefix if present, e.g. 'sha256='). Set to an explicit value to strip that exact prefix (e.g. 'sha256=' for GitHub-style). Services that send plain hex digests without any prefix (e.g. Sentry) should leave this empty or set it to empty string.

max_sessions.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed for this webhook (default: 10)

secret.description: New secret for HMAC signature verification. If not provided, the existing secret is kept.

signature_header.description: Name of the HTTP header containing the signature (default: X-Signature)

signature_prefix.description: Prefix to strip from the signature header value before HMAC comparison. When empty, auto-detection is used.

max_sessions.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed for this webhook (default: 10)

signature_header.description: Name of the HTTP header containing the signature (default: X-Signature)

signature_prefix.description: Prefix to strip from the signature header value before HMAC comparison. When empty, auto-detection is used.

webhook_url.description: URL to configure in GitHub/external service

max_sessions.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed for this webhook (default: 10)

enterprise_url.description: GitHub Enterprise Server URL (empty for github.com)

allowed_events.description: List of allowed GitHub events (empty = all)

go_template.description: Go template expression that evaluates to 'true' or 'false'. Supports both GitHub and custom webhooks. Available functions: contains, hasPrefix, hasSuffix, toLower, toUpper, trimSpace, len, in, matches. Examples: {{ eq .action "opened" }}, {{ contains .pull_request.title "feat:" }}, {{ and (eq .action "opened") (not .pull_request.draft) }}

environment.description: Environment variables for the session. Values can use Go template syntax to extract data from the webhook payload (e.g., {"PR_NUMBER": "{{.pull_request.number}}"})

tags.description: Tags for the session. Values can use Go template syntax to extract data from the webhook payload (e.g., {"pr_number": "{{.pull_request.number}}"})

initial_message_template.description: Go template for initial message (e.g., 'Review PR #{{.pull_request.Number}}')

reuse_message_template.description: Go template for message when reusing existing session (e.g., 'New update for PR #{{.pull_request.Number}}'). If not set, initial_message_template will be used.
